prediction.text:
In its FY2025 10-K risk factors, Johnson & Johnson says the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) has changed Medicare Part D benefit design. It says the IRA has subjected certain of its products to government-established pricing beginning in 2026, and that more products may be subject in the future. J&J also warns of penalty exposure tied to pending litigation, and says Part D changes could hurt U.S. Innovative Medicine sales.
Johnson & Johnson states that the IRA has changed Medicare Part D benefit design and has subjected certain of the Company's products to government-established pricing beginning in 2026, and may subject additional products in the future.
J&J warns that failure to adhere to the government's interpretations of the law, pending ongoing litigation, may expose the Company to penalties.
J&J states that change to Medicare Part D could have a negative impact on U.S. Innovative Medicine sales.

caveats: The IRA discussion is a short paragraph within the broader Item 1A pricing and reimbursement risk factor, not a standalone risk factor. It names no specific drugs and gives no quantified impact.
Only Item 1A of the FY2025 10-K was searched. MD&A and the notes were not reviewed.
